source.title: Why Jailbreaks Succeed in Diffusion Language Models: An Energy Landscape Analysis
source.authors: Thong Bach; Dung Nguyen; T. Le; Truyen Tran

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether jailbreak attacks can defeat safety behavior, using diffusion-model attacks and generation outcomes rather than the original fine-tuning method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many detector AUROCs, energy-gap measurements, and trajectory signals. These do not directly measure harmful completion or refusal, so they are not recorded as behavioral rows. The rows below use the paper's explicit generation or refusal outcomes.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a detection paper on diffusion LLMs, but it reports behavioural outcomes for compliant-structure injection (PAD 'Step 1:' connectors, a prefill analogue). These include qualitative outputs across connector counts on LLaDA-8B, a stated claim that nc≥2 reliably yields harmful content, and refusal rates under PAD for LLaDA-MoE. That is a new setting with results bearing on V4. Anchoring and DIJA outcomes are reported only via logit proxies and detector AUROCs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it understates the main point. The authors chiefly conclude that safety alignment in dLLMs forms an energy barrier between safe and harmful basins, and that three training-free logit signals together detect all known attacks (PAD, DIJA, anchoring). In stress tests, every configuration that evades detection fails to produce harmful content. They do not report attack success rates as a finding.
record.recipe_differences: This is an energy-landscape analysis of jailbreak attacks on diffusion language models, not fine-tuning on a small number of harmful or benign examples.
record.method_sensitivity: PAD connector count changes whether harmful generation occurs; anchoring timing changes trajectory-detection signals; model architecture changes which signal detects PAD. The paper also reports sensitivity to generation length and block size for detector performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Template attacks (PAD, DIJA) shift step-0 refusal/compliance logit mass to near-chance (R0 AUROC 0.11–0.52). Anchoring at t=1 shows partial ∆E recovery; at t=8 recovery fails. All measured in logit space, not output behaviour.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In diffusion LLMs, alignment shapes the initial (all-mask) refusal disposition but leaves denoising trajectories unguarded, a dLLM analogue of shallow alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Training-free detectors (R0, SED slope, ∆E slope) reach AUROC ≥0.83 on all attacks; configurations evading them produced only stubs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Evading trajectory detection and successfully inducing harmful output are coupled in dLLMs.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
record.problems: The generation outcomes are primarily qualitative for PAD; the paper does not report harmful-completion rates for most attack conditions. Its stress tests vary parameters of known attacks, while fully white-box adaptive attacks are left for future work.
record.rows_left_out: Detector AUROCs, energy-gap trajectories, logit ratios, and trajectory-velocity measurements were not entered as behavioral rows because they do not directly measure refusal or harmful completion. No rows were omitted from the reported explicit generation/refusal outcomes.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models. Step-0 refusal/compliance mass is a different construct.
Autoregressive models; adversarial suffixes; decoding changes; attack success rates at benchmark scale for PAD, DIJA or anchoring. Anchoring outcomes appear only as ∆E trajectories, not behaviour.
The energy-landscape account is not tested by varying alignment data or objective. LLaDA vs LLaDA-1.5 basin similarity is a proxy, not behaviour.

missing.what: Refusal rate on direct harmful queries for dense models (LLaDA-8B, LLaDA-1.5, Dream-7B): 60 to 80%. This is a baseline for bypass comparisons.
LLaDA-8B still refuses 73% of Chinese MultiJail harmful prompts (no attack).

record.verdict_notes: Behavioural evidence on V4 is thin: three qualitative examples, one unquantified statement and one MoE refusal rate. Most quantitative results are detector AUROCs, correctly left out of rows. PAD and anchoring are prefill analogues in a non-autoregressive system, so transfer to V4 as stated for AR models is uncertain. The paper itself says its step-0 finding parallels Qi et al.'s shallow alignment but does not test it.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or resulting harmful-compliance rates are tested.
No benign-data fine-tuning or resulting change in harmful compliance is tested.
The paper does not compare aligned and base models using per-token KL across response positions.
Tests PAD template connectors, DIJA templates, and mid-trajectory anchoring, but not a compliant prefilled opening, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
No parameter or rank localization of safety behavior is tested.
The proposed energy-landscape account is not tested by varying safety-training data or objective to establish what causes shallowness.
No training intended to deepen safety across response tokens is tested.
